claims.statement: Article covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and permits repository admins or maintainers to configure publishing; GHES Actions publishing additionally requires site administrator enablement. Role or documentation alone does not establish target permission.

Branch publishing is recommended when build customization is unnecessary; source may be any existing repository branch but folder selection is root or /docs. Source branch pushes describe publication intent, subject to documented trigger exclusions and actual build results.
Custom Actions publishing is recommended for non-Jekyll builds or avoiding a dedicated compiled-output branch; provided templates are examples, not adopted policy or verified deployment.

Branch configuration requires selecting Deploy from a branch, branch and optional folder, then Save. Removing the selected /docs folder causes missing-folder build failure; file or setting existence is not publication evidence.

Repositories containing symbolic links require Actions publishing according to the included note. This does not authorize symbolic links in the final Pages archive; the companion workflow guide excludes symbolic and hard links there.

Branch publication troubleshooting calls for a push by an admin with a verified email. Commits pushed by an Actions workflow using GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger a Pages build; token availability must not be mistaken for successful triggering.

The build-pages-with-actions conditional applies to FPT/GHEC: even external-CI sites deploy through Actions; external CI commonly commits output and .nojekyll to gh-pages, allowing deploy-only execution. Do not generalize this conditional to all GHES versions.

Build/deployment troubleshooting examines actual workflow runs and optional reruns; documentation links or rerun instructions do not constitute observed success or authorization to execute a deployment.

Selecting Actions as source can use an existing workflow or suggested template. Pages settings are not bound to one specific workflow and show the most recent deploying run; effective workflow identity requires the actual deployment receipt.

The described general workflow triggers on default-branch push or manual invocation, checks out content, optionally builds static files, and uploads a Pages artifact. The text specifies default-branch-push deployment and PR deployment skipping; it does not fully specify manual-trigger deployment conditions.

Templates create github-pages environment automatically if absent and recommend restricting deployment to the default branch. Creation or environment reference is distinct from installed protection and tested rejection of unauthorized deployment.

In the FPT/GHEC custom-workflow context a repository CNAME file does not automatically add or remove the custom domain; repository settings or API configuration is required. This is not a universal claim about branch-source behavior.
Private repository visibility does not itself prove private Pages publication; included product-specific warnings and plan availability must remain separate from effective site access.

Source procedures describe native settings and publishing operations, not an approval to mutate this estate. All extracted claims remain reference-only; live published assurance, policy acceptance, rights and rollout evidence remain outstanding.
